This is actually a really impossible question to answer with just one game but for this time around I will shine the spotlight on ADOM: Ancient Domains Of Mystery.

It started out as a small ascii rougelike on DOS way back in the day when games like Zork were still around. Today it is one of the most complex, open and feature filled games of all time.

The first truly open world game ever as far as I know, it's a turn based fantasy with countless weapons, armors, spells, potions, scrolls, food, morality, religion. Around 12 different races to choose from that offer vastly different gameplay and on top of that about 24 different classes.

Originally it had a VERY steep learning curve and you needed to use your entire keyboard but these days it uses a system called 'NotEye' to make use of the mouse and simplify a lot of things. It also has graphical tiles these days but thankfully it still has the option of ascii graphics as nothing beats your imagination in this type of game.

It's definitely not for everyone and not necessarily my favorite of all time but it is a game that I consider to be one of the greatest ever made and was WAY ahead of it's time.
